answer:
### How to Set Up Google Client ID and Secret for Gmail

To connect Gmail in Pigeon using **Google sign-in (OAuth)** instead of app passwords, you need your own **Google Cloud OAuth client** and to add **Client ID** and **Client Secret** in Pigeon. Your plan must allow Gmail (e.g. Premium).

**Step 1: Get credentials from Google Cloud Console**
1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create or select a project → **APIs & Services** → **Credentials**.
3. Click **+ Create Credentials** → **OAuth client ID**.
4. If prompted, set up the OAuth consent screen (External, app name e.g. Pigeon, support email).
5. For the client: choose **Web application**, name it (e.g. "Pigeon Gmail").
6. **Important:** Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, **copy the URI from Pigeon** — go to **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**, open the form where you add credentials, and copy the **Authorized redirect URI** shown there. Paste it into Google Cloud (do not type it manually).
7. Save. Copy the **Client ID** (e.g. `xxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com`) and **Client Secret** (e.g. `GOCSPX-xxxxx`). The secret is shown only once.

**Step 2: Save in Pigeon**
1. In Pigeon: **Settings** → **Integrations** → **Gmail**.
2. Paste **Google Client ID** and **Google Client Secret**.
3. Click **Save**, then **Connect with Google** to add your Gmail account as an inbox.

**Quick tips:** If you see "Redirect URI mismatch", the URI in Google Cloud must match exactly — always copy from Pigeon. If the app isn’t verified, you can choose Advanced → Go to Pigeon to continue during testing.

### How to Connect Gmail with an App Password (Without OAuth)

You can connect Gmail to Pigeon using a **Google App Password** — a 16-character password from Google that lets Pigeon send and receive email without your main Gmail password. Your plan must allow Gmail; add accounts from **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**.

**Before you start**
- Your Gmail account must have **2-Step Verification** turned on (Google only issues App Passwords for accounts with 2-Step Verification).
- Generate the App Password from your Google Account, not from Pigeon.

**Step 1: Turn on 2-Step Verification (if needed)**
1. Go to [Google Account](https://myaccount.google.com/) → **Security**.
2. Under "How you sign in to Google," open **2-Step Verification** and follow the steps (phone or authenticator app).

**Step 2: Create an App Password**
1. **Security** → **2-Step Verification** → scroll to **App passwords**.
2. Select app **Mail**, device **Other** (e.g. "Pigeon").
3. Click **Generate**. Copy the 16-character password (spaces optional); you won’t see it again.

**Step 3: Add Gmail in Pigeon**
1. Pigeon → **Settings** → **Integrations** → **Gmail**.
2. Click **Connect via App Password**.
3. Enter your **Gmail address** and paste the **App Password**.
4. Click **Connect**. The account appears under **Inbox Accounts** and in Settings → Integrations → Gmail.

**Troubleshooting:** "Invalid credentials" usually means 2-Step Verification is off or you used your normal password — use the App Password only. If "App passwords" is missing, enable 2-Step Verification first.

### How to Add and Verify Your Sending Domain in Pigeon

To send from your own domain (e.g. you@yourcompany.com) instead of Gmail, you need to **add and verify** the domain in Pigeon by adding DNS records at your domain provider. Once verified, you can add SMTP inboxes and use them in campaigns. Go to **Domains** in the sidebar to start.

**Step 1: Add your domain**
1. Click **Domains** in the left sidebar → **Add Domain**.
2. Enter your domain (e.g. **yourcompany.com**) — no http:// or www.
3. Save. Pigeon will show the DNS records you need.

**Step 2: Add DNS records**
You’ll typically need:
- **SPF** — TXT record that authorizes Pigeon to send for your domain.
- **DKIM** — One or more TXT records for authentication.
- **MX** (if receiving) — So replies reach your inbox.

1. In Domains, select your domain and copy each record (Type, Name/Host, Value).
2. Log in to your DNS provider (GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap, etc.) and add each record exactly as shown.
3. Save. Propagation can take a few minutes up to 48 hours.

**Step 3: Verify**
1. Back in Pigeon → **Domains** → select your domain → **Verify**.
2. If it fails, check that every record matches exactly (no extra spaces) and wait for propagation.

**After verification:** Add **Inbox Accounts** (SMTP) for addresses on this domain and choose **SMTP** when creating campaigns.

### How to Set Up Reply-To (IMAP) for Campaign Replies

**Reply-To** controls where replies to your campaign emails go. You can send them to a specific Gmail or IMAP mailbox that Pigeon monitors, so replies show up in the **Inbox** tab. Set this in **Settings → Integrations**.

**Step 1: Set default reply-to**
1. Go to **Settings** → **Integrations** → find **Reply-To** or **Campaign replies**.
2. Choose **Use sending inbox** (replies to the sender) or **Specific Gmail / IMAP**.
3. For Gmail: pick the connected account from the dropdown.
4. For a custom domain mailbox: add an **IMAP** config first (see below), then select it.
5. Save. You can override this per campaign when creating or editing it.

**Step 2: Add Reply-To IMAP (optional)**
If replies go to an address not connected as Gmail (e.g. support@yourdomain.com):
1. In **Settings → Integrations**, find **Reply-To IMAP** or **IMAP configs**.
2. Click **Add** / **Add IMAP account**.
3. Enter **Email**, **IMAP host** (e.g. imap.yourprovider.com), **Port** (usually 993), **Username**, **Password** (or app password).
4. Save. Pigeon tests the connection. Then you can select this mailbox as reply-to so replies appear in the Inbox.

**Per campaign:** When creating/editing a campaign, look for **Reply-To** or **Reply to address** and set a different address if needed.

**Troubleshooting:** If replies don’t show, ensure the reply-to address is one Pigeon can read (Gmail connected or IMAP added) and that the campaign uses that reply-to. IMAP failed? Check host, port, username, and password; many providers need an app password.

### How to Add SMTP Inbox Accounts for Your Domain

SMTP inboxes let you send campaigns from your own domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com). You add them **after** your domain is **verified** in **Domains**. Each SMTP inbox uses credentials from your email provider (SendGrid, your host, etc.).

**Before you start**
- Verify your domain in **Domains** (DNS records + Verify).
- Have SMTP details ready: host, port, username, password (or API key). Your provider’s docs or support can give these.

**Step 1: Open Inbox Accounts**
1. Click **Inbox Accounts** in the sidebar → **Add Inbox** or **New inbox**.

**Step 2: Choose SMTP and domain**
1. Select **SMTP** or **Domain inbox** (not Gmail).
2. Select your **verified domain**. Only verified domains appear.
3. Enter the **email address** for this inbox (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com) on that domain.

**Step 3: Enter SMTP credentials**
1. **SMTP host** (e.g. smtp.sendgrid.net or mail.yourprovider.com).
2. **Port** (often 587 for TLS or 465 for SSL).
3. **Username** and **password** (or API key).
4. Use **Test connection** / **Verify** if available, then Save.

The new inbox appears in **Inbox Accounts** with status like **Warming** or **Ready**. In **Campaigns**, choose **SMTP** as sender and select this inbox.

**Troubleshooting:** Domain not in list → verify in Domains and refresh. Connection failed → check host, port, username, password and TLS/SSL. New SMTP inboxes may need warmup before full sending — check the Warmup section.

answer:
### Understanding Inbox Status: Ready, Warming, and Warm Up Required

Each sending inbox has a **status** that tells you whether it’s safe to use for campaigns and how much you can send. Sending too much from a new or cold inbox can hurt deliverability. Check status in **Inbox Accounts** and **Warmup**.

**What each status means**
- **Ready** — Inbox is warmed or doesn’t need warmup. Use it in campaigns up to your plan and daily limits. Ideal for sending.
- **Warming** — Warmup in progress. You can often use it at a reduced rate; check the Warmup page for limits. Sending more than the curve can hurt reputation.
- **Warm up required** — Inbox is new or warmup not started. Start warmup from the **Warmup** page before full campaigns. Full volume from this state is risky.
- **Warning** — Warmup below a safe threshold. Consider pausing campaigns using this inbox or increasing warmup.
- **Paused** — Warmup or sending paused. Resume from Warmup or inbox settings when ready.

**Where you see it**
- **Inbox Accounts** — Status badge on each inbox.
- **Warmup** — Timeline and per-inbox progress; start, pause, resume.
- **Campaigns** — Warnings when selecting inboxes that aren’t ready.

**What to do:** Ready → use normally. Warming → stay within suggested limits. Warm up required → start warmup first. Warning → improve warmup or reduce sending.

answer:
### What Is Email Warmup and How to Use It in Pigeon

**Email warmup** is gradually increasing how much you send from a new or unused inbox so providers (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) learn to trust it. Sending a lot right away can get mail flagged as spam. Warmup sends a controlled amount (often to internal or partner addresses) and builds a positive pattern so your real campaigns land in the inbox.

**In Pigeon** (on supported plans) the **Warmup** feature warms Gmail and SMTP inboxes before you use them. The **Warmup** page in the sidebar shows which inboxes are warming, their progress, and lets you start, pause, or resume warmup.

**How to use it**
1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. You’ll see inboxes and their state: not started, warming, paused, or complete.
3. For **Warm up required** or **Start warmup**: click **Start** or **Enable warmup** for that inbox.
4. Progress appears on the Warmup page and in **Inbox Accounts**. When status becomes **Ready** or **Warming** (within limits), you can use it in campaigns.
5. **Pause** from the Warmup page or inbox settings; **Resume** when you’re ready.

**Best practices:** Start warmup for new inboxes before campaigns. Don’t send large volume from "Warm up required" or early "Warming". Use recommended send limits for warming inboxes. Keep warmup running until Ready for best deliverability.

questions: How to Start, Pause, or Resume Warmup for Your Inboxes
answer:
### How to Start, Pause, or Resume Warmup for Your Inboxes

You control warmup from the **Warmup** page in the sidebar. It lists your inboxes (Gmail and SMTP) with each one’s warmup state and progress, and you can turn warmup on or off per inbox.

**Start warmup**
1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. Find the inbox that shows **Warm up required**, **Not started**, or **Start warmup**.
3. Click **Start**, **Enable warmup**, or the equivalent for that inbox.
4. Warmup begins. Status in **Inbox Accounts** may change to **Warming**, and the Warmup page shows progress (timeline or %).

**Pause warmup**
1. Go to **Warmup** → find the inbox that is **Warming**.
2. Click **Pause** (or **Pause warmup**) for that inbox.
3. Warmup stops; the inbox may show **Paused**. You can resume later.

**Resume warmup**
1. Go to **Warmup** → find the inbox with **Paused** or **Resume warmup**.
2. Click **Resume** (or **Resume warmup**).
3. Warmup continues from where it left off; progress updates on the Warmup page and in Inbox Accounts.

**Note:** Pigeon sends a controlled volume from that inbox over time. You don’t need to run campaigns during warmup. When the inbox reaches the target level, status in **Inbox Accounts** becomes **Ready** and you can use it for campaigns.

### How to Check Warmup Progress and When Your Inbox Is Ready

Warmup progress is in two places: the **Warmup** page (sidebar) and **Inbox Accounts**. The Warmup page has the timeline and per-inbox progress; Inbox Accounts shows a short status and often a percentage or "Warmed" per inbox.

**On the Warmup page**
1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. For each inbox with warmup enabled you’ll see **Progress** (e.g. % or progress bar), **Timeline** (sending over time), and **Status** (Warming, Paused, Complete/Ready).
3. When progress hits the target (e.g. 100% or your plan’s threshold), the inbox is ready and its status in **Inbox Accounts** usually changes to **Ready**.

**On Inbox Accounts**
- Each inbox has a **status** badge (Ready, Warming, Warm up required, Warning, Paused) and often a **warmup** value (e.g. "65% warmed" or "Warmed").
- **Ready** (and sometimes a high %) = you can use it for campaigns within plan limits. **Warming** = use only within the suggested warmup limits.

**When is my inbox ready?**
- **Ready** — Safe for full campaign volume (within daily and plan limits).
- **Warming** with high % — Often OK at reduced volume; check in-app notes for limits.
- **Warm up required** or **Warning** — Not ready; keep warmup running or fix the issue before sending campaigns.

### How to Import Contacts from CSV or Excel

Campaigns are sent to **contact lists**. You can build those lists by importing from a CSV or Excel file (e.g. from your CRM or a spreadsheet). Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar, then **Import** to upload and map columns.

**Step 1: Prepare your file**
- One row per contact; columns for email and any other fields (first name, last name, company, etc.).
- **Email** is required; others optional. Formats: **.csv**, **.xlsx**, **.xls**. Max size usually **10 MB**.
- Need a template? Use **Contacts → Import** and download the **example CSV** from the import page.

**Step 2: Start the import**
1. **Contacts** (sidebar) → **Import** (or **Import contacts**).
2. **Upload file** — select your CSV or Excel file or drag and drop. The app reads the first rows and shows detected columns.

**Step 3: Map columns**
- Match your file’s column headers to Pigeon fields (Email, First name, Last name, Company, Industry, Location). **Email** must be mapped.
- Choose **Add to existing list** or **Create new list** (and name it).

**Step 4: Save and review**
- Click **Import** or **Save**. Pigeon processes the file and adds contacts to the chosen list.
- Check the summary (how many imported, any errors). Fix issues (e.g. invalid emails) in your file and re-import if needed.
- The list appears under **Contacts** and can be selected when creating a campaign.

### How to Map Columns When Importing Contacts

**Column mapping** tells Pigeon which column in your file is which contact field (Email, First name, Company, etc.). Your file might use "Email Address" or "E-mail"; mapping links that to Pigeon’s **Email** field so imports work correctly.

**Where it happens**
- After you upload a file in **Contacts → Import**, you get a **mapping** step with your file’s column names and a dropdown of Pigeon fields for each.

**Pigeon fields you can map**
- **Email** (required) — The contact’s email.
- **First name**, **Last name**, **Company**, **Industry**, **Location** — Optional; map only if your file has them.

**How to map**
1. For **Email**, choose the column with email addresses (e.g. "Email", "E-mail", "Email Address"). Required.
2. For **First name**, **Last name**, **Company**, etc., select the matching column or leave unmapped.
3. Columns that don’t match any field stay unmapped and won’t be imported.
4. Double-check Email — wrong mapping can cause failed imports or bad data.
5. Continue to the next step (choose list, then Import).

**Tips:** Use the **example CSV** on the import page for recommended headers. Ensure the first row is column names, not data. Don’t map the same file column to more than one Pigeon field.

### How to Manually Block or Unblock Contacts

You can **block** a contact so they never get campaigns from you (e.g. unsubscribes, invalid addresses, or people who asked to be removed). **Unblocking** adds them back so they can receive campaigns again. Pigeon has **Manual Block / Unblock** under **Contacts** for this.

**Where to do it**
1. Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar.
2. Open **Manual Block / Unblock** (may be under a submenu or tab under Contacts).
3. You’ll see options to block or unblock, often by entering an email or choosing from a list.

**Block a contact**
1. In **Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock**, find the **Block** section or form.
2. Enter the contact’s **email** (or select from a list if the UI allows).
3. Confirm or click **Block**. They’re added to the block list and won’t receive future campaigns (and may be excluded from existing ones depending on how sends are processed).

**Unblock a contact**
1. In **Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock**, find the **Unblock** section or list of blocked contacts.
2. Find the contact (e.g. by email) in the blocked list.
3. Click **Unblock** or **Remove from block list**. They can receive campaigns again if they’re in a list you use.

The Manual Block / Unblock page usually shows currently blocked emails so you can review and unblock as needed.

### How to Use Verified Leads (Pro)

**Verified Leads** is a Pro feature that focuses on contacts whose email addresses have been verified (e.g. double opt-in or verification step). That can improve deliverability and engagement by sending only to valid, engaged addresses. It’s under **Contacts** when your plan includes it.

**Where to find it**
1. Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Verified Leads** (may be under a submenu like "Contacts → Verified Leads").
3. You’ll see a list or view of contacts marked as verified.

**How it works**
- Contacts are marked **verified** when they confirm their email (e.g. link in a verification email) or through your verification flow.
- The Verified Leads view filters or highlights these contacts so you can build lists or segments from them.
- When creating campaigns, use a contact list that contains only or mostly verified leads for better deliverability.

**Using verified leads in campaigns**
1. Make sure you have contacts in the verified leads list (from signup or a verification step).
2. Create a **contact list** that includes your verified leads, or use one built from verified-leads data.
3. When creating a campaign, select that list as the audience so you’re sending mainly to verified addresses.

### How to Use Merge Variables (first_name, company)

**Merge variables** are placeholders in templates that are replaced with each contact’s data when the campaign runs. For example, {{first_name}} becomes "John" for one contact and "Jane" for another. That personalization improves opens and replies. Available variables depend on the **contact list** you use — they come from that list’s fields (e.g. from your import or CRM).

**Common merge variables**
- **{{first_name}}** — First name
- **{{last_name}}** — Last name
- **{{email}}** — Email address
- **{{company}}** — Company name
- **{{industry}}**, **{{location}}** — If you have these fields

Your list may have more custom fields; **Templates → Template Guide** or **Template Prompts** list the exact variables for the list you use in a campaign.

**Where to use them**
- **Subject:** e.g. "Hi {{first_name}}, one question about {{company}}".
- **Body:** e.g. "Hi {{first_name}}," or "I saw that {{company}} is in {{industry}}."
- Only use variables that exist on your contact list; missing fields may show blank or a default.

**How to insert**
- When editing a template (**Templates** → select or New), type the variable in double curly braces: {{first_name}}, {{company}}, etc.
- Or use the editor’s insert/list option for available merge variables.

**Spintax (optional):** Some plans support {Option A|Option B|Option C} for random variation per email. Check the Template Guide for syntax.

questions: How to Add an Unsubscribe Link for Compliance
How do I add unsubscribe link?
answer:
### How to Add an Unsubscribe Link for Compliance

An **unsubscribe** option is required for compliance (e.g. CAN-SPAM, GDPR) and helps reduce spam complaints. Pigeon lets you add an **unsubscribe link** placeholder in templates; when the campaign runs, it’s replaced with a real link so contacts can opt out. You can also enforce this in **Settings → Compliance**.

**Add the placeholder in your template**

2. In the **body**, add a line such as:
   - "Unsubscribe: {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}" or
   - "To stop receiving these emails, unsubscribe here: {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}"
3. The exact placeholder may vary by plan; check **Templates → Template Guide** (e.g. {{unsubscribe_url}} or {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}).
4. Save. When you use this template in a campaign, Pigeon replaces the placeholder with the working unsubscribe link.

**Enable "require unsubscribe" in Compliance**
1. **Settings** (sidebar) → **Compliance** tab.
2. Find **Require unsubscribe link** (or similar) and turn it **on** so templates or campaigns without an unsubscribe link are blocked or warned.
3. Save.

**Where to place the link**
- Usually at the **bottom** of the email (e.g. after your signature).
- Use clear wording: "Unsubscribe", "Manage preferences", or "Stop receiving these emails" with the link.
- One unsubscribe link per email is usually enough; don’t hide it or use tiny font.

questions: How to Create Your First Campaign in Pigeon
How do I create my first campaign?
What do I need before campaign?
answer:
### How to Create Your First Campaign in Pigeon

A **campaign** in Pigeon is an outreach sequence: you choose a **contact list**, one or more **email templates** (with delays between steps), and **sending inboxes** (Gmail or SMTP). Pigeon sends according to your schedule and daily limits. Create campaigns from **Campaigns** in the sidebar.

**Before you start**
- At least one **contact list** with contacts (Contacts → Import or create list).
- At least one **email template** (Templates → create with subject, body, merge variables, unsubscribe).
- At least one **inbox** ready (Gmail or SMTP in Inbox Accounts, status Ready or within warmup limits).

**Step 1: New campaign** — **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Create campaign**.

**Step 2: Info and audience** — Campaign name (e.g. "Q1 cold outreach"), select **contact list**, set **timezone**.

**Step 3: Sender** — Choose **Gmail** or **SMTP**, select one or more **inboxes** (must be Ready or allowed). Optionally set **sender rotation** (e.g. round-robin) if you have multiple inboxes.

**Step 4: Email sequence** — Add one or more **steps**. For each step: select a **template** and set a **delay** (e.g. 0 days for the first, 2 days for the second). The first email goes when the campaign runs; follow-ups go after the delay.

**Step 5: Schedule and limits** — **Daily limit** (e.g. 50/day), **send time window** (e.g. 9:00–17:00). Optionally set **reply-to** (default from Settings or a specific Gmail/IMAP).

**Step 6: Launch** — Review and click **Launch** or **Start campaign**. Monitor under **Campaigns** (sent count, replies) and **Inbox** for replies.

questions: How to Choose Gmail vs SMTP and Select Sending Inboxes

### How to Choose Gmail vs SMTP and Select Sending Inboxes

When creating or editing a campaign, you choose how to send: **Gmail** (accounts connected in Settings → Integrations) or **SMTP** (domain inboxes added in Inbox Accounts after verifying your domain).

**Gmail** — Quick to set up; good for personal or small-team outreach. Connect via OAuth or App Password in **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**. Each connected account is an inbox you can select in the campaign.

**SMTP** — Send from your own domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com). Verify the domain in **Domains** and add SMTP inboxes in **Inbox Accounts**, then select those inboxes when the sender type is SMTP.

**How to choose in a campaign**
1. **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** → find **Sender** or **Sending from**.
2. Select **Gmail** or **SMTP**:
   - **Gmail** — List shows all connected Gmail accounts. Select one or more; campaign sends from these (with rotation if multiple).
   - **SMTP** — You may select a **domain** first, then one or more SMTP inboxes for that domain. Use only **Ready** (or allowed) inboxes.
3. With multiple inboxes, set **sender rotation** (e.g. round-robin or random) to spread sends.

**Tips:** Use **Ready** inboxes; avoid **Warm up required** or **Warning** unless you stay within warmup limits. For small lists, fewer inboxes can be better for reputation; for large lists, more inboxes help with daily limits. Use **test send** (if available) to confirm the selected inbox works before launch.

questions: How to Set Daily Limits and Send Time Windows
How do I set daily limit?
answer:
### How to Set Daily Limits and Send Time Windows

**Daily limits** cap how many emails a campaign sends per day so you don’t overload inbox reputation or hit provider limits. **Send time windows** (e.g. 9:00–17:00) ensure emails go out only during business hours in the recipient’s timezone, which can improve opens and replies. You set both when creating or editing a campaign.

**Where to set them**
- **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** → find **Schedule**, **Sending**, or **Limits** (often after contact list and inboxes).

**Daily limit**
- Enter the maximum emails this campaign can send per day (e.g. 50 or 100). The campaign stops for the day once this is reached and continues the next day.
- This usually applies to the campaign as a whole (across all selected inboxes). Keep it within your plan and warmup recommendations.

**Send time window**
- **Start time** and **End time** — When emails can be sent (e.g. 09:00 to 17:00). Only contacts whose local time falls in this window receive emails then.
- **Timezone** — Set the campaign timezone (e.g. America/New_York). Pigeon uses this (and the contact’s timezone if available) to send within the window.
- Sends are typically spread across the window, not all at once.

**Best practices:** Start with a conservative daily limit (e.g. 30–50) for new inboxes; increase as reputation builds. Use business-hour windows (e.g. 8–18) in the recipient’s region for better engagement.

questions: How to Run Template A/B Tests in a Campaign
How do I run A/B test in campaign?
answer:
### How to Run Template A/B Tests in a Campaign

**A/B testing** in a campaign means sending two (or more) versions of an email (e.g. different subject lines or bodies) to parts of your audience and comparing performance (opens, replies). Pigeon supports this so you can see which template performs better. The exact controls depend on your plan; look for **A/B test** or **Template A/B Testing** when creating or editing a campaign or a sequence step.

**Where to set it up**
- **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** → in the **email sequence** section, when you add or edit a step, look for **A/B test** or **Variants** (e.g. "Add variant" or "Test subject A vs B"). You may also see A/B under **Get Started** in the "Template A/B Testing" section.

**How to run an A/B test**
1. For the step you want to test, add **two (or more) variants**: e.g. Template A (subject A) and Template B (subject B), or two different templates.
2. Set the **split** (e.g. 50% / 50%) so part of the audience gets variant A and part gets B.
3. Launch the campaign. Pigeon sends the variants according to the split.
4. After sends, check **Analytics** or **Campaign** stats to compare opens, replies, or other metrics for each variant. Use the better-performing variant for future templates.

**Best practices:** Test one thing at a time (e.g. subject only, or body only) so results are clear. Use a large enough audience so the split gives meaningful numbers. Run the test for a set period or until you have enough data, then use the winner for future campaigns.

questions: How to Edit or Pause a Campaign
How do I edit a campaign?

questions: How to View and Manage Campaign Replies in the Inbox

questions: How to Use the Inbox to See When Contacts Respond

questions: How to Use Sending Behavior (Tracking) to Improve Deliverability
answer:
### How to Use Sending Behavior (Tracking) to Improve Deliverability

**Sending Behavior** (or **Tracking**) in Pigeon shows how you’re sending over time: volume, distribution by hour, by inbox, and by campaign. It helps you spot patterns that can hurt deliverability (e.g. sending too much at once or from one inbox only) so you can adjust and improve inbox placement. Open it from **Sending Behavior** or **Tracking** in the sidebar.

**What you see** — **Charts** (sends over time, e.g. last 7 days, by day and hour). **By inbox** (which inboxes sent how many; balance sending across inboxes). **By campaign** (which campaigns sent how many; avoid one campaign dominating). **Insights** — Some plans show tips (e.g. "Spread sends across more hours" or "Reduce peak rate").

**How to improve deliverability**
1. **Spread sends** — If most emails go out in one hour, providers may treat it as bulk. Use **daily limit** and **send time window** in campaigns to spread sends across the day.
2. **Balance inboxes** — If one inbox sends much more than others, add more inboxes or rotate senders so no single inbox is overloaded.
3. **Stay within warmup** — For warming inboxes, keep volume within the recommended limits shown in Warmup and Inbox Accounts.
4. **Use the data** — Check Sending Behavior regularly (e.g. weekly); if you see spikes or imbalance, adjust campaign limits or send windows.

Use **Sending Behavior** (Tracking) to see send volume and distribution; spread sends over time and across inboxes to improve deliverability.

questions: Why Your Gmail Connection Fails and How to Fix It
answer:
### Why Your Gmail Connection Fails and How to Fix It

When **Connect Gmail** or adding a Gmail account fails in Pigeon, it’s usually due to credentials, security settings, or plan limits. Here are the most common causes and fixes.

**1. Invalid credentials (App Password)** — Symptom: "Invalid credentials" or "Authentication failed". **Fix:** Use an **App Password**, not your normal Gmail password. In Google Account → Security → 2-Step Verification → App passwords, generate a new App Password for Mail / Other (Pigeon) and paste it into Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect via App Password). Ensure 2-Step Verification is on; without it, App Passwords aren’t available.

**2. Google OAuth credentials not set** — Symptom: "Google OAuth credentials not set" or you can’t use "Connect with Google". **Fix:** An admin must add **Google Client ID** and **Client Secret** in Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail). See our guide on setting up Google Client ID and Secret. After they’re saved, try Connect with Google again.

**3. Redirect URI mismatch (OAuth)** — Symptom: After signing in with Google, "Redirect URI mismatch" or "Error 400". **Fix:** In Google Cloud Console, the **Authorized redirect URI** for your OAuth client must match **exactly** the URI shown in Pigeon when you add credentials (Settings → Integrations → Gmail). Copy the URI from Pigeon and paste it into Google Cloud; don’t type it by hand. Then try connecting again.

**4. Plan limit reached** — Symptom: "You have reached the Gmail limit for your plan". **Fix:** Your plan allows only a certain number of Gmail accounts. Disconnect an unused Gmail in Settings → Integrations → Gmail, or upgrade your plan.

**5. App not verified (OAuth)** — Symptom: Google shows "This app isn’t verified". **Fix:** For testing, choose **Advanced** → **Go to Pigeon (unsafe)** to continue. For production, consider submitting your app for Google verification.

questions: Redirect URI Mismatch: How to Fix Google OAuth Errors
Authorized redirect URI copy from Pigeon
answer:
### Redirect URI Mismatch: How to Fix Google OAuth Errors

When you use **Connect with Google** (OAuth) in Pigeon, Google redirects the user back to your app after sign-in. The **redirect URI** is the URL Google sends them to. If that URL doesn’t **exactly** match one of the **Authorized redirect URIs** in your Google Cloud OAuth client, Google shows an error (e.g. "Redirect URI mismatch" or "Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch").

**Why it happens** — The URI in Google Cloud was typed by hand and has a typo or wrong path; or it uses http instead of https (or wrong domain/port); or Pigeon’s callback URL changed and Google wasn’t updated.

**How to fix it**
1. **Get the exact URI from Pigeon** — **Settings** → **Integrations** → **Gmail** → open the form where you enter **Google Client ID** and **Client Secret** (or "Add your Google OAuth credentials"). On that page, Pigeon shows the **Authorized redirect URI** you must use. Copy it exactly (including https, domain, and path).
2. **Update Google Cloud Console** — Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) → **APIs & Services** → **Credentials** → click your **OAuth 2.0 Client ID** (Web application). Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, add the URI you copied from Pigeon (or replace the wrong one). No extra spaces or characters. Save.
3. **Try again** — In Pigeon, click **Connect with Google** again. Sign-in and redirect should complete without the mismatch error.

**Important:** Copy from Pigeon; don’t type. The URI must match character for character. If you have multiple environments (e.g. staging vs production), each has its own redirect URI; add each one in Google Cloud if you use both.

questions: Best Practices for Inbox Warmup Before Sending Campaigns
answer:
### Best Practices for Inbox Warmup Before Sending Campaigns

Sending a lot from a **new or cold inbox** can hurt deliverability; providers may treat it as spam. **Warmup** gradually builds sender reputation so your real campaigns are more likely to land in the inbox. Follow these practices for best results.

**Start warmup early** — Add new Gmail or SMTP inboxes in **Inbox Accounts**, then go to **Warmup** and **start warmup** for each new inbox. Don’t launch large campaigns from an inbox that’s still **Warm up required** or early **Warming**. Wait until status is **Ready** (or follow the recommended limits for warming inboxes).

**Respect warmup limits** — While an inbox is **Warming**, Pigeon (or your plan) may suggest a maximum daily send. Stay at or below that so the warmup curve isn’t disrupted. Use **Inbox Accounts** and **Warmup** to see progress; only increase campaign volume when the inbox is ready.

**Use multiple inboxes wisely** — Spreading volume across several warmed inboxes is better than overloading one. Add more inboxes and use **sender rotation** in campaigns (round-robin or random). For small lists, fewer inboxes can be easier to manage and still safe if they’re fully warmed.

**Don’t pause and rush** — If you **pause** warmup, resume when ready; don’t send at full volume as soon as you resume. Let warmup continue to **Ready** before scaling campaigns. Avoid big bursts from a single inbox; use **daily limits** and **send time windows** in campaigns to spread sends.

**Monitor and adjust** — Check **Sending Behavior** (Tracking) and **Analytics** for send volume per inbox. If one inbox sends much more than others, balance by adding more inboxes or adjusting campaign sender selection. If you get **Alerts** about deliverability or reputation, slow down or pause campaigns and ensure warmup is complete for the affected inboxes.

### Understanding Alerts: Deliverability and System Notifications

**Alerts** in Pigeon are notifications about **deliverability** and **system** issues: e.g. a domain or inbox problem, a campaign issue, or a recommendation to act. They help you fix problems before they affect your sending. Open **Alerts** from the sidebar.

Some alerts may also appear on the **Dashboard** or as a badge on the Alerts item (e.g. unread count).

**Types of alerts** — **Success**: something completed (e.g. domain verified, campaign finished). **Warning**: something to watch (e.g. warmup progress low, high bounce rate). **Error**: something failed (e.g. inbox connection failed, domain verification failed). **Info**: general information or tips.

**What to do** — **Read the message** (it usually explains what happened and which resource is affected). **Take action**: e.g. fix DNS if domain verification failed; reconnect or fix credentials if an inbox failed; pause a campaign or improve warmup for a deliverability warning. **Mark as read** (if available) to track what you’ve handled. You can **delete** old alerts to keep the list clean.

**Deliverability vs system** — Deliverability alerts relate to domains, inboxes, warmup, bounces, or reputation; act on these so your emails keep landing in the inbox. System alerts relate to the app (e.g. maintenance, feature changes); read for context; no action may be needed.

questions: Understanding Gmail Sending Limits: OAuth vs App Password
How many emails per day Gmail?
answer:
### Understanding Gmail Sending Limits: OAuth vs App Password

Google applies **daily sending limits** to each Gmail account. If you exceed them, emails may bounce or your account can be restricted. Pigeon respects these limits. The limit depends on **how** you connect: OAuth (sign-in with Google) or App Password.

**OAuth (Connect with Google) — ~500 per day** — When you connect Gmail via **OAuth** (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect with Google), you use the Gmail web/API channel. For **personal Gmail** (@gmail.com), Google typically allows around **500 recipients per day** per account. This is the higher limit and is best for outreach volume.

**App Password — ~100 per day** — When you connect via **App Password** (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect via App Password), Pigeon uses SMTP/IMAP. For personal Gmail, Google typically allows around **100 recipients per day** per account. Use this when you prefer not to use OAuth.

**What Pigeon does** — **Per-inbox limits:** you can set a daily limit per inbox (e.g. 50). We never send more than your configured limit or Google’s cap. **New inboxes:** for inboxes newer than 7 days or near their daily cap, we use a safer sending pattern. **Reset time:** per-inbox limits reset at **midnight UTC**. Plan your campaign daily limits and send windows accordingly.

**Tips:** Prefer **OAuth** if your plan supports it for higher daily volume per Gmail. Use **multiple Gmail accounts** (within your plan limit) and spread volume. Start with a **low daily limit** (e.g. 50) and increase gradually; Google may adjust limits based on your sending behaviour.

questions: How Per-Inbox Daily Limits Work (Reset Time, New Inboxes)
Per inbox limit how it works
answer:
### How Per-Inbox Daily Limits Work (Reset Time, New Inboxes)

Each **sending inbox** in Pigeon can have a **daily send limit** (e.g. 50 emails per day). This protects deliverability by capping how much one inbox sends in 24 hours. Pigeon also applies a **safer pattern** for new or at-cap inboxes.

**Reset time** — Per-inbox limits **reset at midnight UTC** every day. After reset, the "sent today" count for that inbox goes back to 0 and the inbox can send again up to its daily limit. Your **campaign** daily limit and **send time window** (e.g. 9–17 in your timezone) still apply; we only send during that window and never exceed the campaign or per-inbox cap.

**New inboxes (<7 days)** — For inboxes **newer than 7 days**, Pigeon uses a **safer sending pattern**: we avoid maxing out the daily limit and may use longer gaps between sends. This helps build reputation. Once the inbox is older and warmed (e.g. status **Ready**), you can rely on the full daily limit within your campaign settings.

**Near daily cap** — When an inbox is **near its daily cap** (e.g. 48/50 sent today), we may slow or stop using it for the rest of the day and use other inboxes in the rotation. After midnight UTC, that inbox is available again.

**Where you see this** — **Inbox Accounts**: each inbox shows **Sent today** (or similar). **Campaigns**: the campaign’s **daily limit** is the total across all selected inboxes; we distribute sends and respect each inbox’s per-inbox limit and reset. **Sent tooltip**: on campaign or inbox views, the (?) or info icon explains rotation, human-like timing, and daily limits.

questions: Campaign Daily Limit vs Per-Inbox Limits: How They Work Together
How do campaign and inbox limits work together?
Campaign limit total per inbox limit
answer:
### Campaign Daily Limit vs Per-Inbox Limits: How They Work Together

When you run a campaign, two limits apply: the **campaign daily limit** (total emails per day for that campaign) and the **per-inbox daily limit** (max each inbox can send per day). Pigeon enforces **both** so you never exceed either.

**Campaign daily limit** — Set when you create or edit a campaign (e.g. 100 emails per day). This is the **total** that campaign can send in one day across **all** selected inboxes. We spread sends across the send time window (e.g. 9–17) and rotate across inboxes (round-robin or random).

**Per-inbox daily limit** — Each **inbox** has its own daily cap (e.g. 50 per day), set in Inbox Accounts or when adding the inbox. No single inbox will send more than its per-inbox limit in one day (reset at midnight UTC). If you have 2 inboxes with 50 each and a campaign limit of 100, we can send up to 100 that day (50 + 50). If one inbox already sent 50, we use only the other until the next day.

**How they work together** — We **never** send more than the **campaign** daily limit in one day. We **never** send more than each inbox’s **per-inbox** limit in one day. So effective daily send = min(campaign limit, sum of available per-inbox capacity). Example: campaign 200, two inboxes 50 each → we send at most 100 that day (50 + 50).

**Tips:** Set **campaign** limit to match your goals; set **per-inbox** limits to protect each inbox’s reputation. Use enough inboxes so that the sum of their per-inbox limits is at least your campaign limit if you want to hit the campaign cap every day.

questions: Domain Verification Failed: Common Fixes (SPF, DKIM, MX)
answer:
### Domain Verification Failed: Common Fixes (SPF, DKIM, MX)

**Domain verification** in Pigeon checks that the right **DNS records** (SPF, DKIM, MX) are present for your domain. If verification fails, it’s usually because a record is missing, wrong, or not yet propagated. Fix the records and try **Verify** again.

**Check the exact values** — In **Domains**, select your domain and open **DNS records** or **Verification**. Pigeon shows the **exact** Type, Name/Host, and **Value** you must add. Copy them exactly — no extra spaces, no typos. At your **DNS provider** (e.g. Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap), open DNS management for this domain and compare each record.

**SPF (TXT)** — Only **one SPF (TXT) record** per domain (or subdomain) is allowed. If you already have an SPF record, you must **merge** Pigeon’s include (e.g. `include:sendgrid.net` or similar) into your existing SPF value. Do not create two separate SPF TXT records. Format is usually: `v=spf1 include:... ~all` or `-all`. Add Pigeon’s include inside the same string.

**DKIM (TXT)** — DKIM is usually one or more **TXT** records with a specific **name** (e.g. `pigeon._domainkey` or what Pigeon shows) and a long **value**. Copy name and value exactly. Some providers want the value in one line; others allow multiple lines — follow the provider’s UI.

**MX (if required)** — If Pigeon asks for **MX** records (e.g. for receiving), add the **priority** and **value** (e.g. `mx.sendgrid.net`) as shown. Don’t remove existing MX records if you need them for receiving email elsewhere; you may need to add Pigeon’s MX with a lower priority or adjust according to your setup.

**Propagation** — DNS changes can take **minutes to 48 hours** to propagate. If you just added records, wait 15–30 minutes and click **Verify** again. If it still fails, double-check values and try again later.

questions: Understanding Campaign and Inbox Health Scores
answer:
### Understanding Campaign and Inbox Health Scores

Pigeon may show a **health score** (e.g. 0–100) for **campaigns** and **inboxes**. This score reflects how well the campaign or inbox is doing from a **deliverability and reputation** perspective: sending pattern, bounce/complaint signals, warmup state, and similar factors. A higher score is better.

**Where you see it** — **Campaigns** list or **campaign detail**: a campaign may have a health score badge or tooltip. **Inbox Accounts** or **Warmup**: an inbox may show a health or reputation indicator. **Health score tooltip**: hover or click the (?) or info icon next to the score to see a short explanation of what affects it.

**What affects the score** — **Sending volume**: sending too much too fast (especially from new or cold inboxes) can lower the score. **Warmup**: inboxes that are **Ready** or well warmed tend to have better scores; **Warm up required** or **Warning** can reduce it. **Bounces and complaints**: high bounce or spam complaint rates can lower the score. **Consistency**: steady, human-like sending (daily limits, send windows, rotation) tends to support a good score.

**What to do** — **Green / high**: keep doing what you’re doing; stay within daily limits and send windows. **Amber / medium**: review Sending Behavior and warmup; consider lowering daily limit or pausing campaigns until warmup improves. **Red / low**: reduce sending from that campaign or inbox, ensure warmup is running or complete, and fix any bounce/complaint issues (e.g. list hygiene, block list).

questions: How to Add Multiple Steps and Follow-up Delays to a Campaign
How do I add follow-up steps?
answer:
### How to Add Multiple Steps and Follow-up Delays to a Campaign

A **campaign** in Pigeon is an **email sequence**: one or more **steps** (emails) sent to each contact. The **first** step is usually sent when the contact enters the campaign (or when the campaign runs); **follow-up** steps are sent after a **delay** (e.g. 2 days, 5 days). You add steps and set delays when creating or editing the campaign.

**Where to add steps** — **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** → open the **Email Sequence** (or **Sequence**) step/tab. You’ll see a list of steps (e.g. Step 1, Step 2). Each step has a **template** (subject + body) and a **delay** (e.g. 0 days, 2 days, 5 days).

**Add a step** — Click **Add step** or **Add email** (or the + icon). Select a **template** for this step (existing or create in Templates). Set the **delay**: 0 for the first email (sends immediately when the contact is due), or e.g. 2 for "send 2 days after the previous step." Delays are usually in **days**; the system schedules the next step relative to when the previous one was sent. Save. Repeat to add more follow-ups (e.g. Step 1: 0 days, Step 2: 2 days, Step 3: 5 days).

**Reorder or remove** — **Reorder**: drag steps or use up/down to change the order. The first step (delay 0) is the initial email; the rest are follow-ups. **Remove**: delete a step you don’t need. Contacts who already received that step are unaffected; those who haven’t will skip it.

**Best practices:** Keep the **first** step delay at **0**. Use **2–5 days** between follow-ups so you don’t look spammy. Use **merge variables** and **unsubscribe** in every template. Run **compliance check** before launching.

questions: How to Use Spintax in Email Templates
answer:
### How to Use Spintax in Email Templates

**Spintax** (spin syntax) lets you define **multiple options** for a word or phrase; when the email is sent, **one option is picked at random** per recipient. That way each contact gets a slightly different line (e.g. "Hi" vs "Hello" vs "Hey") so your copy feels more natural and less template-like. Pigeon supports Spintax in both **subject** and **body** of templates.

**Syntax** — Use **pipe-separated options** inside **curly braces**: `{Option A|Option B|Option C}`. For each send, one of the options is chosen. Example: `{Hi|Hello|Hey} {{first_name}},` → one recipient gets "Hi John,", another "Hello Jane,", another "Hey Alex,". Subject: `{Quick question|One thing}| about {{company}}` → random first part, then the merge variable.

**Where to use it** — **Subject line**: vary the opening or call-to-action (e.g. `{Re: Intro|Following up}| {{first_name}}`). **Body**: greetings, transitions, or CTAs (e.g. `{Hope you're well|Just reaching out|I wanted to connect}.`). **With merge variables**: you can mix (e.g. `{{first_name}}, {thanks|thank you} for your time.`).

**Best practices:** **Don’t over-spin** — a few spins per email add variety; too many can look odd or trigger filters. **Keep options similar in length and tone** so readability and compliance (spam words, link count) stay consistent. **Test** — send a few test emails or preview with sample data to see how spins look. **Compliance:** Spintax is evaluated after merge variables. Make sure **no option** contains spam words or exceeds link/image limits (Settings → Compliance). The Template Guide and compliance check apply to the final content.

questions: How do I duplicate a campaign?
answer:
### How to Duplicate a Campaign

**Duplicating** a campaign creates a **copy** with the same settings (contact list, sequence, inboxes, daily limit, send window, reply-to). You can then change the name, tweak the sequence or audience, and launch it as a new campaign without re-entering everything. Useful for running similar outreach to a different list or A/B testing a variant.

**Where to duplicate** — **Campaigns** (sidebar) → find the campaign you want to copy → use the **Duplicate** action (e.g. from the row menu, three dots, or a Duplicate button). Click it.

**What gets copied** — **Campaign name** (usually with a suffix like "(Copy)" or you can rename when editing). **Contact list** (you can change it when editing the duplicate). **Email sequence** (all steps: templates + delays). **Sender** (Gmail or SMTP and the same inbox selection). **Schedule** (timezone, send time window, daily limit). **ReplyFlow** (reply-to setting).

**What to do after duplicating** — The new campaign appears in the list, usually in **Draft** status. Open it and **Edit** to change the name, switch the contact list, or adjust the sequence before launching. When ready, **Start** or **Launch** the campaign.

**Notes:** Duplication does **not** copy **tracking data** (opens, clicks, replies) or **send history** — only the configuration. You’re subject to **plan limits** (max campaigns); if you’re at the limit, you must upgrade or pause/delete another campaign before duplicating.

questions: Understanding Campaign Jobs and How to Stop a Send
How do I stop a send?
answer:
### Understanding Campaign Jobs and How to Stop a Send

When a campaign **runs**, Pigeon processes sends in **jobs** (batches). Each job has a status: **Pending**, **Running**, **Completed**, **Failed**, or **Cancelled**. You can see active and recent jobs on the **Campaign Actions** (or **Jobs**) page for that campaign and, if needed, **stop** a running job so no more emails go out from that batch.

**Where to see jobs** — **Campaigns** → open a campaign (click its name) → **Actions** or **Jobs** (e.g. Campaigns → [Campaign name] → Actions). You’ll see a list of jobs: status, start time, progress (e.g. sent count), and actions (e.g. **Stop** for a running job).

**Stop a running job** — Find the job with status **Running**. Click **Stop** (or **Cancel** / **Stop job**). Confirm if prompted. The job stops; no further emails are sent for that batch. Contacts who already received an email from that job are unaffected; those still in the queue for that job will not receive it unless a new job is started.

**When to stop a job** — You launched the campaign by mistake and want to halt immediately. You noticed a wrong template, list, or inbox and want to fix the campaign before more sends. You hit a limit or got an alert and want to pause sending.

**After stopping** — The campaign may still show as **Running** if other jobs are pending. **Pause** the campaign from the campaign detail page to stop all future sends. Edit the campaign (sequence, list, inboxes) as needed, then **Resume** when you’re ready, or leave it paused.

questions: How to Edit an Existing Email Template
How do I edit a template?
answer:
### How to Edit an Existing Email Template

**Where to edit** — **Templates** (sidebar) → Template Management → find the template you want to change → click it or **Edit** / pencil icon. You’ll open the **template editor** with the current name, subject, and body.

**What you can change** — **Name**: so you can find the template easily (e.g. "Cold outreach – intro v2"). **Subject line**: update the subject; you can add or change merge variables (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}) and Spintax. **Body**: update the email body (plain text or HTML). Keep or add merge variables and the **unsubscribe** placeholder (see Template Guide for the exact placeholder).

**After saving** — **Campaigns already using this template** will send the **updated** subject and body for **future** sends (e.g. follow-up steps that haven’t been sent yet). Already-sent emails are unchanged. If you run **compliance check** (spam words, links, images), fix any issues before saving so existing and new campaigns stay compliant.

**Best practices:** Don’t remove the **unsubscribe** line; it’s required for compliance. Use **Templates → Template Guide** for merge variables and compliance limits. If you want to keep the old version, **duplicate** the template first (if the option exists), then edit the copy.

### Warmup Credit Settlement (Reply-Based)

Warmup credits now settle based on **reply detection**.

**How it works** — When someone rents a warmup listing, credits move to **held** first. If a **reply** is detected on that send, held credits are released to the provider. If no reply is detected within roughly **48 hours**, the renter is refunded and the held amount expires.

**Important** — Warmup credit qualification no longer depends on tracking-pixel opens or click-tracking links.

**Where to monitor** — Use Warmup logs and Rent credits/activity to see held, released, and refunded outcomes.

### Understanding Pigeon Plans and Pricing

**Where to see plans and pricing** — **Pricing page**: from the marketing site or **Pricing** in the footer/menu you can see available plans (e.g. Free, Pro, Premium), features, and price. **Settings → Billing**: inside the app you see your **current plan**, **usage** (e.g. inboxes used, campaigns, Gmail accounts), and **limits**. You can upgrade or manage subscription here (or via the link provided).

**What plans typically include** — **Inboxes**: max sending inboxes (Gmail + SMTP). **Gmail (Google accounts)**: max Gmail accounts you can connect; some plans allow 0 (SMTP only). **Campaigns**: max campaigns (active + paused + draft). **Domains**: max verified domains (varies by plan). **Warmup**: whether inbox warmup is included and how many inboxes can be warmed. **Templates, contacts, analytics**: usually included; limits may apply (e.g. contact list size).

**Upgrade and downgrade** — **Upgrade**: from Settings → Billing (or Pricing), choose a higher plan. You may be charged a prorated amount or at the next billing cycle. **Downgrade**: if you switch to a lower plan, you may need to stay within the new limits (e.g. remove extra inboxes or campaigns). The app or billing page will explain when the change takes effect.

**Trial and refunds** — **Free trial**: some plans offer a trial; check **Get Started** or **Pricing** for eligibility. When the trial ends, you may be moved to Free or asked to subscribe. **Refunds**: see the **Refund** or **Terms** page (footer) for the refund policy.

questions: Contact Import: File Size, Format, and Duplicate Handling
answer:
### Contact Import: File Size, Format, and Duplicate Handling

**File format and size** — **Supported formats**: **.csv**, **.xlsx**, **.xls**. One row per contact; first row is usually headers (column names). **Max file size**: typically **10 MB**. If your file is larger, split it into multiple files or reduce columns/rows and import in batches. **Encoding**: use UTF-8 when possible so special characters (accents, symbols) import correctly.

**Required and optional columns** — **Email** is **required**. Every row must have a valid email address; invalid or empty emails may be skipped or cause the row to fail. **Optional**: First name, last name, company, industry, location, and custom fields. Map them in the import step (Contacts → Import → map columns to Pigeon fields).

**Duplicate handling** — **Same email in the file**: if you have duplicate emails in the same file, the importer may keep one and skip the rest, or update the same contact (depending on app behaviour). Check the import summary after upload for "Imported" vs "Skipped" or "Updated." **Email already in the list**: when you add contacts to an **existing list**, contacts whose email is already in that list may be **skipped** (not duplicated) or **updated** (if you have update-on-import). The import result shows how many were added vs skipped. **Across lists**: the same email can exist in **different** contact lists; each list is independent. A contact is not automatically removed from another list when you import into a new list.

**Tips:** **Download the example CSV** from the import page to see the recommended format and headers. **Remove invalid emails** before importing to avoid high skip counts. **Back up** important lists before large imports or overwrites.

questions: How do I reset my password?
answer:
### How to Reset Your Password

If you **forgot your password** or want to **change it** for security, use the **Forgot password** flow. Pigeon will send you an email with a link to set a new password.

**Step 1: Request a reset link** — On the **Login** page, click **Forgot password?** (or the equivalent link). Enter the **email address** associated with your Pigeon account. Click **Send** or **Reset password**. If that email is in our system, you’ll receive a message with a **reset link** (valid for a limited time, e.g. 1 hour).

**Step 2: Set a new password** — Open the email and click the **reset link**. You’ll be taken to a **Reset password** page (or Set new password). Enter your **new password** (and confirm it if the form has two fields). Use a strong password: mix of letters, numbers, and symbols; avoid common words. Submit. Your password is updated; you can now **log in** with the new password.

**If you don’t receive the email** — Check **spam** and **promotions** folders. Ensure you entered the same email you use to log in. Wait a few minutes; delivery can be delayed. Try again once; avoid requesting many resets in a short time (rate limits may apply). If it still fails, contact **Support** (Tickets) with your account email so we can help.

**After resetting** — **Log in** with your email and the **new** password. If you use **sessions** or "Remember me," you may need to log in again on some devices after a password change.
